headline: This 2023 law creates a National Heritage Area System, sets rules for designating new areas, and orders feasibility studies for proposed areas in Hawaii, Virginia, and North Carolina.
what_it_does: The law sets up a National Heritage Area System made up of existing heritage areas and any added later by Congress. The Interior Department may give technical and financial help to local groups that run these areas. Only an act of Congress can designate a new National Heritage Area, and these areas are not treated as National Park System units. The law also orders studies for the proposed Kaena Point and Great Dismal Swamp areas, renames Iowa's America's Agricultural Heritage Partnership as Silos & Smokestacks, and extends some management plan deadlines.

who_it_affects.group: Local coordinating entities that run National Heritage Areas
who_it_affects.how: They may receive federal technical and financial assistance from the Interior Department to establish and maintain their areas.

who_it_affects.group: Communities near the proposed Kaena Point area in Hawaii
who_it_affects.how: Interior must study whether the area should be designated as a National Heritage Area.

who_it_affects.group: Communities near the proposed Great Dismal Swamp area in Virginia and North Carolina
who_it_affects.how: Interior must study whether the area should be designated as a National Heritage Area.

who_it_affects.group: Partners in Iowa's America's Agricultural Heritage Partnership
who_it_affects.how: The heritage area is renamed Silos & Smokestacks National Heritage Area.

who_it_affects.group: Managers of certain existing heritage areas
who_it_affects.how: The law extends the deadline for submitting their management plans.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on January 5, 2023. The official summary does not list other specific effective dates.
